conn_claude_intro: Add PostQueen as a connector and Claude can read your calendar, draft posts and schedule them without you leaving the chat.
conn_chatgpt_intro: ChatGPT connectors speak MCP, so PostQueen appears as a tool it can call while you talk to it.
conn_n8n_intro: Use the community node to publish from an n8n flow, and PostQueen webhooks to trigger a flow when a post publishes.
conn_n8n_step_cred_detail: Create a PostQueen credential in n8n and paste your API key into it.
conn_n8n_step_trigger_detail: Add your n8n webhook URL under Settings → Webhooks. PostQueen posts the published post to it.
connections_sub: Work with PostQueen across your favorite tools.
conn_step_skill_install_detail: One command, once per machine. It brings the postqueen CLI with it.
conn_step_skill_key_detail: The agent reads this from the environment. Put it in your shell profile to make it permanent.
conn_step_mcp_url_detail: PostQueen speaks Model Context Protocol over streamable HTTP. The key travels in the URL.
conn_claude_short: Draft, schedule and publish from a Claude conversation.
conn_claude_note: For Claude Code in a terminal, the Agent Skills route below is usually better — it loads context on demand instead of the whole schema up front.
conn_claude_step_settings_detail: Claude → Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector.
conn_claude_verify: Ask Claude to list your connected channels. It should name every one.
conn_chatgpt_short: Manage your content from ChatGPT with a custom connector.
conn_chatgpt_note: Custom connectors need a ChatGPT Plus, Pro or Business plan.
conn_chatgpt_step_settings_detail: Settings → Connectors → Add, then choose a custom connector.
conn_chatgpt_verify: Ask ChatGPT for your PostQueen account details.
conn_gemini_short: Connect Gemini CLI to your PostQueen workspace.
conn_gemini_intro: Gemini CLI reads MCP servers from its settings file.
conn_cc_short: Register PostQueen with Claude Code in one command.
conn_cc_intro: Claude Code can take PostQueen either as an MCP server or as an Agent Skill. MCP is one command; skills load less context per call.
conn_editors_name: Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf, Warp, Amp
conn_editors_short: Every MCP-capable editor takes the same server.
conn_editors_intro: These all read an MCP config file. Developers → Access generates the exact snippet for each one, including the file it belongs in.
conn_editors_step_url: Point your editor at the server
conn_editors_step_url_detail: Most take a URL plus an Authorization header.
conn_editors_step_auth_detail: Send the key as a bearer token, or use the URL that carries it if your editor cannot set headers.
conn_openclaw_short: A personal agent that can post for you — from your terminal or your phone.
conn_openclaw_intro: OpenClaw is an open-source agent you run yourself. It reads the Agent Skills package rather than MCP, which means it loads PostQueen's commands on demand instead of carrying a whole tool schema in every prompt — cheaper, and it leaves room for the rest of your context.
conn_openclaw_note: The same install also powers the chat bridge below: once OpenClaw has this skill, anything that can reach your agent can publish through it. Keep a human in the loop before anything goes out.
conn_openclaw_verify: Ask the agent to list your social accounts. It should name every channel you have connected.
conn_hermes_short: Register PostQueen as a Hermes tool provider.
conn_hermes_intro: Hermes is Nous Research's open-source agent framework. It picks PostQueen up through the same Agent Skills package the other CLI agents use, so one install covers every agent on the machine.
conn_codex_short: Post from your terminal through Codex.
conn_codex_intro: Codex discovers PostQueen from the skill definition and runs its commands in a sandbox.
conn_bridge_short: Message an agent from your phone and it posts for you.
conn_bridge_intro: OpenClaw runs a gateway on your own machine or server that connects chat apps to an AI agent. Give that agent the PostQueen skill and you can schedule a post by sending a message — from WhatsApp, Slack, Discord, Telegram, Signal and around two dozen others.
conn_bridge_note: The gateway is yours: it runs on your infrastructure and PostQueen never sees your chat accounts. Keep a human in the loop before anything publishes.
conn_bridge_step_gateway_detail: Follow OpenClaw's own setup, then connect the chat apps you want from its channels list.
conn_bridge_step_try_detail: From any connected chat app, in your own words.
conn_bridge_example: Schedule this to LinkedIn and X tomorrow at 9am: …
conn_n8n_short: Publish from a workflow, or start one when a post goes out.
conn_n8n_note: Self-hosted n8n needs the community node installed before the credential appears.
conn_zapier_short: Connect 7,000+ apps through the API and webhooks.
conn_zapier_intro: There is no PostQueen app in Zapier's directory yet. Until there is, Zapier's own generic steps do the job in both directions.
conn_zapier_step_out_detail: Create a "Catch Hook" trigger in Zapier, then paste its URL under Settings → Webhooks. Every published post arrives there.
conn_zapier_step_in_detail: Use the "Webhooks by Zapier" action with POST and this URL to create a post.
conn_zapier_step_auth_detail: Add this header to the action.
conn_make_intro: No PostQueen module yet. Make's HTTP and Webhooks modules cover the same ground.
conn_make_step_out_detail: Add a Custom Webhook module, copy its URL and paste it under Settings → Webhooks.
conn_make_step_in_detail: Use the HTTP "Make a request" module against the public API.
conn_make_step_auth_detail: Add an Authorization header holding your API key.
conn_api_short: A REST API for channels, posts, media and analytics.
conn_api_intro: Everything the app does to your account, you can do over HTTP: list channels, schedule and delete posts, upload media, generate video, read analytics.
conn_api_step_auth_detail: Send your key in the Authorization header on every request.
conn_api_step_post_detail: POST to /posts with the channels and the content.
conn_cli_short: Drive PostQueen from a terminal or a CI job.
conn_cli_intro: The CLI prints JSON, so anything that can run a shell command can run your publishing.
conn_cli_step_login_detail: Interactively, or set POSTQUEEN_API_KEY in CI.
conn_sdk_short: A typed client for Node applications.
conn_sdk_intro: A thin wrapper over the public API with types for the request and response shapes.
conn_sdk_step_key_detail: Pass your API key when you construct the client.
conn_webhooks_short: Get told when a post publishes.
conn_webhooks_intro: PostQueen POSTs the published post as JSON to any URL you register. A webhook can watch every channel or just the ones you pick.
conn_webhooks_note: Requests are not signed, so treat the URL itself as the secret — give each destination its own, and do not act on a payload you cannot otherwise verify.
conn_webhooks_step_add_detail: Settings → Webhooks. Optionally limit it to certain channels.
conn_webhooks_step_receive_detail: A POST with the post, its channel and its release URL, once publishing succeeds.
conn_oauth_short: Publish on behalf of other PostQueen accounts.
conn_oauth_intro: If you are building a product rather than automating your own account, register an OAuth app. Your users authorise it and you receive a token that works with the API, MCP and the CLI — no key sharing.
conn_oauth_step_create_detail: Developers → Apps. Set your redirect URL there.
conn_oauth_step_token_detail: Tokens are prefixed pos_ and go in the same Authorization header as an API key.
guide_instagram: Connects through Facebook, which is where Instagram keeps its publishing permissions.
guide_instagram_req: The account must be a Business or Creator account and linked to a Facebook Page. A personal Instagram account cannot be published to by any tool.
guide_instagram_standalone: Connects to Instagram directly, without going through a Facebook Page.
guide_instagram_standalone_req: Still needs a Business or Creator account.
guide_x: Connects the X account you are currently signed in to.
guide_x_req: Switch accounts on X first if you want a different one — this cannot be chosen during the connect.
guide_youtube: Connects a YouTube channel through your Google account.
guide_youtube_req: The Google account must already own a channel. Google will let you sign in without one and the connect will then have nothing to attach to.
guide_gmb: Connects a Google Business Profile location.
guide_gmb_req: The location has to be verified. Unverified locations do not accept posts.
guide_tiktok: Connects your TikTok account for scheduled posting.
guide_tiktok_req: TikTok reviews new posting apps per account; the first post may need to be made public from the app before scheduling works.
guide_pinterest: Connects Pinterest so posts land on a board you choose.
guide_pinterest_req: You need at least one board before anything can be scheduled.
guide_linkedin_page: Connects a LinkedIn company page rather than your personal profile.
guide_linkedin_page_req: You must be an admin of the page.
guide_reddit_req: Each subreddit has its own posting rules and flair requirements — those are chosen per post, not here.
guide_mastodon: Connects a Mastodon account on any instance.
guide_slack: Posts into a Slack channel you pick during the connect.
guide_discord: Adds a bot to a Discord server so it can post to a channel there.
guide_discord_req: You need Manage Server permission on the server you pick.
guide_bluesky: Bluesky uses an app password — a separate password you create for tools, which you can revoke without changing your own.
guide_bluesky_req: Two-factor authentication is not supported yet. If it is on, turn it off before connecting.
guide_bluesky_s2: Create one, give it a name you will recognise, and copy it.
guide_bluesky_s3: Paste your handle and that app password below — not your account password.
guide_bluesky_f_service: Leave as bsky.social unless you are on your own instance.
guide_bluesky_f_password: The app password you just created.
guide_devto: DEV publishes through an API key you generate in your account settings.
guide_devto_s2: Scroll to DEV Community API Keys, name a key and generate it.
guide_devto_s3: Copy it once — it is not shown again.
guide_hashnode: Hashnode publishes through a personal access token.
guide_hashnode_s2: Generate a new token and copy it.
guide_medium: Medium publishes through an integration token from your account settings.
guide_medium_req: Medium stopped issuing new integration tokens in January 2025 and no longer allows new integrations. Tokens created before then still work — so if you already have one, paste it. If you have never made one, Medium will not give you one now.
guide_wordpress: Publishes to a self-hosted WordPress site over its REST API.
guide_wordpress_req: Use an application password, not your login password. WordPress will reject the login password.
guide_wordpress_s1: In WordPress admin, open Users → Profile.
guide_wordpress_s2: Scroll to Application Passwords, add one and copy the generated value.
guide_wordpress_f_domain: The site root, for example https://example.com
guide_wordpress_f_pass: The application password, spaces and all.
guide_listmonk: Sends to a Listmonk mailing list on your own server.
guide_listmonk_f_url: Your Listmonk root URL, for example https://mail.example.com
guide_listmonk_f_pass: That user's API token, from Listmonk → Settings → API users.
guide_lemmy: Posts to communities on a Lemmy instance.
guide_lemmy_f_service: The instance URL, for example https://lemmy.world
guide_nostr: Signs and broadcasts notes with your Nostr key.
guide_nostr_req: The key must be in HEX form. An nsec1… key has to be converted first — a client such as iris.to will show you the hex version.
guide_nostr_f_key: Your private key in HEX. It is stored encrypted, but treat it as you would any key that can post as you.
guide_telegram: Connects a Telegram channel or group through a short code exchange rather than a redirect.
guide_telegram_req: Add the bot to the channel and make it an administrator, otherwise it cannot post.
guide_wrapcast: Connects a Farcaster account by signing with your wallet.
guide_wrapcast_req: You will be asked to sign a message. Signing proves the account is yours; it does not move funds.
guide_moltbook: Connects Moltbook by signing with your wallet.
guide_moltbook_req: You will be asked to sign a message. Signing proves the account is yours; it does not move funds.
guide_skool: Skool has no public API, so posting goes through the PostQueen browser extension using your own logged-in session.
guide_skool_req: The extension has to be installed and you have to be signed in to Skool in the same browser.
guide_default: You will be sent to {{name}} to sign in and approve access. Nothing is posted until you schedule it.
conn_openclaw_try_detail: In your own words — it works out the channels, the media and the timing.
conn_openclaw_example: Post the blog cover to LinkedIn and X tomorrow at 9am, and draft a thread for Bluesky
conn_hermes_note: Hermes can run tools on a schedule from its own config, which is a neat fit for recurring publishing — a weekly digest, say. Whatever you automate, keep a human in the loop before it publishes.
conn_hermes_try_detail: Hermes discovers your channels first, then schedules.
conn_hermes_example: Schedule my latest post to every connected channel for Monday morning
